title: Usage discrepancy resolution & retroactive credit playbook for enterprise invoices
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers hit edge-case invoice disputes where usage on an invoice doesn't match the customer's expectation due to a combination of (a) model-version token counting changes, (b) retries/streaming partial-charges counting twice, (c) seat-based prorations + usage tiers interaction, and (d) retro-committed discounts or contract soft-caps. These disputes lead to manual billing adjustments, slow resolution SLA, and churn risk for large accounts.

Goal: Create a product + ops playbook and a minimal automation prototype to resolve usage discrepancies quickly and consistently. The playbook should define detection heuristics, triage steps, automated credit rules, audit trails, and escalation paths tied to contract terms. It should also provide a measurable experiment to evaluate automation vs. manual outcomes (time-to-resolution, dollar impact, and CSAT).

Scope: Enterprise invoices (monthly/quarterly), cases flagged by customers or billing anomaly detector where discrepancy >= $100 or >= 5% of invoice. Exclude simple tax/VAT corrections and card failures. Deliverables: (1) documented playbook, (2) a one-click credit generator in Console for ops, (3) backend rule prototype that proposes credits for common causes, (4) SLO for dispute resolution time and audit logging, (5) A/B experiment plan to test automation.

Constraints & considerations: Must respect signed contract terms (grace periods, caps, overage policies). Credits must be auditable and reversible. Automations must not violate revenue recognition rules; finance must sign off on thresholds. Integration with enterprise security questionnaire: explain auditability, RBAC, and change logs for credits.

Key trade-offs considered: conservative auto-credit thresholds reduce false positives but increase manual handling; broad heuristics reduce ops time but risk financial exposure. We will start conservative and iterate based on experiment signals.

Finance sign-off received on credit thresholds and revenue recognition implications
